assertions.notes: Recommends `WithAccessible(true)` and describes it as replacing the interactive form with plain, one-line-at-a-time prompts.
Says a terminal app can't reliably detect a screen reader, and adds an ACCESSIBLE env var, an `--accessible` flag and a saved config setting.
Explains that constant repainting and cursor jumps make NVDA read fragments or repeated text, and that the selection shows only as a redrawn highlight.
Advises keeping the rest of the app plain text, but never says Bubble Tea itself has no screen-reader support.
Never suggests making every onboarding answer settable through flags or config so the form can be skipped entirely.
Recommends Huh's accessible mode via `.WithAccessible(accessible)`, which replaces the TUI with plain sequential prompts.
Says NVDA can't be reliably detected and offers a `--accessible` flag, an ACCESSIBLE env var and a saved config setting.
Explains that the cursor-movement redraws reach NVDA as a jumble of redrawn fragments, and that highlight is only a color or `>` character, which is why linear prompts work better.
Advises plain output in the rest of the app when accessible, but never states that Bubble Tea itself has no screen-reader support.
Recommends a non-interactive path such as `mycli init --name foo --region us-east-1 --yes` so users can skip the prompts entirely.
Recommends Huh's built-in accessible mode via `.WithAccessible(accessible)`, which replaces the TUI with plain one-per-line prompts.
Makes the mode opt-in through an `ACCESSIBLE=1` env var, a `--accessible` flag and a saved config setting, and notes that screen-reader detection is unreliable.
Explains that the form repaints regions in place and moves the cursor, so NVDA reads stale fragments or misses the focused item, which is why plain prompts work better.
Advises giving the rest of the app plain output under the same setting, but never states that Bubble Tea itself has no screen-reader support.
Recommends exposing every onboarding field as a flag (e.g. `mycli init --name … --region …`) so there is a fully non-interactive path.
Section 3 says to give every TUI action (filter, drill in, restart) a non-TUI path through flags, subcommands, or a line-by-line prompt.
It replaces table rows with labelled sentences, one item per line, and adds a separate `--format json` or `csv` option.
The answer never says to send results to stdout and prompts, progress, or diagnostics to stderr.
It uses a summary status line in words and appended change lines, and explicitly bans `\r` progress bars and spinners.
It converts color to words like 'failing', arrows to 'rising', and bans ANSI codes and box-drawing characters; labels remove reliance on column position.
It recommends an environment variable or config setting (e.g. `MYAPP_NO_TUI=1`) so users don't have to pass the flag every time.
Section 3 requires an equivalent for every key-driven TUI action (filter, sort, drill in, acknowledge) through flags, subcommands or a line-based prompt.
It replaces table rows with labelled records such as 'Service api-1: degraded. CPU 42 percent.' and adds `--format json` (or csv).
It sends errors to stderr and renders to stdout, but never says prompts or progress output should go to stderr.
It reports status in words with a summary line, appends timestamped event lines, and rules out spinners, `\r` overwrites and screen clears.
It explains that meaning carried by color, glyphs and alignment is lost, and calls for words instead of color or glyphs and no box-drawing characters or sparklines.
It suggests setting the mode once in a config file or env var (e.g. `DASH_PLAIN=1`) and turning it on automatically for non-TTY output or `TERM=dumb`.
Section 3 says every TUI action (filter, drill in, ack, restart) needs a non-TUI equivalent via subcommands, so plain mode isn't read-only.
It recommends one item per line as `label: value` and offers `--json` as a separate machine format.
It only says to send errors to stderr; it never says results go to stdout while prompts and progress go to stderr.
It reports status as words (a summary line and event lines in watch mode) and explicitly rules out spinners, progress bars and cursor movement.
It says to write status as words rather than color alone, to turn glyphs and sparklines into words, and to drop box-drawing and column alignment.
It suggests a config setting or an environment variable like `DASH_NO_TUI=1` so the mode can be enabled persistently.
